<reason>CON won a competitive, high-clarity clash by making the decision rule easier: non-linear tipping, choke-point vs capillary enforcement, and irreversibility showed spreading creates first-time losses without rescuing the core. PRO’s leak, leftover-residents, and “volume vs who pays” frames stayed live but never neutralized that weighing. A clipped CON opening is a real cost, not enough to flip the round.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2 answers to PRO’s pressure: visitors belong in an already-tipped core because damage is thresholded, and dispersal demands the capillary enforcement the overload already proves cities lack.</best_rebuttal>
